newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer spending demands restraining tax rises.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer spending demands restraining tax rises.

text.p: A leap in British consumer credit in May rammed home the message to Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown that personal tax rises are needed to take the heat out of high street spending, analysts said on Monday.
Bank of England figures showed consumer credit leapt by 1.105 billion stg last month, while April's increase was revised up to 806 million from an initial 691 million.
The figures are particularly well timed with Brown due to unveil his first budget in just two days' time.

"Consumer credit is growing at a pretty frenetic pace," said Kit Juckes, head of bond and currency strategy at NatWest Markets. "The only question is how much of an interest rate rise and how much of a consumer tax rise we're going to see."

Money supply figures released at the same time showed M0, the narrow money supply measure, rose a provisional, seasonally adjusted 6.3 percent in the year to June. That was above most economists' forecasts which centred on a 6.0 percent increase.
Final M4 data for May showed the broader measure rose an unrevised 11.1 percent year-on-year in May, well above the government's three-to-nine percent monitoring range.
But it is consumer credit that will be of prime concern to the Chancellor and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.

Even though base rates have been raised in two quarter-point notches to 6.5 percent since Labour came to power on May 1, George and his now-independent monetary policy committee will not hesitate to tighten policy further if Brown is deemed not to have taken sufficient action in Wednesday's budget.

"We're getting a very consistent message, consumers are spending merrily," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. He said much of the wave of demand washing through the high streets may be in response to a flood of windfall payments from building societies converting into banks.
Halifax Plc, Britain's largest mortgage lender, has already handed out shares worth about 17 billion pounds and a total of about 35 billion is expected over the summer.
